thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager duty alert: P1 - elevated egress failures from ca-central1 affecting inference egress. Trigger: 5xx_rate > 5% for 3m across regional NAT clusters. Pager: oncall-sre.
maria (oncall-sre): On it. I'm inside the gateway dashboards now. Anyone seeing matching Cloud NAT errors?
wayne (netops): Confirming. ca-central1 egress to upstream provider AS34300 showing TCP RST/connection resets. Error rate ~11% last 7m. No obvious instance CPU mem issues.
wayne (netops): BGP sessions look flappy to one of our peers in the region, other peers healthy.
maria (oncall-sre): Paging netops to own route-level mitigation. Oliver/eng-runtime - are there in-flight inference jobs we should drain or redirect?
oliver (eng-runtime): We have continuous batches on a handful of dedicated pools in ca-central1. We'll prepare to fail traffic to ca-west1 and eu-south1; need a short window to swap routing and validate cache warm-up.
sarah (product): Triage question: which customers are affected? Dan can you start collecting impacted accounts with active sessions in ca-central1?
dan (cust-succ): I'll pull active API keys from the traffic filters and start outreach templates. Want me to hold messages until we have a status page blurb?
emma (legal): Keep any external wording conservative — don't speculate on root cause. Use 'network provider instability' if needed.
maria (oncall-sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Netops to advertise more-specific routes to divert egress via alternate peer for ca-central1, 2) Eng-runtime to activate route failover policy to ca-west1 for non-pin customers, 3) Send initial status page "investigating" update. Can netops confirm they can push route changes now?
wayne (netops): Pushing route change to peer2 now. Will monitor BGP convergence. ETA ~60s for converge.
statusbot: Status update posted draft -> [status.redwood.example/incidents/2245001234] (private edit).
maria (oncall-sre): Eng-runtime, roll failover?
oliver (eng-runtime): Starting traffic diversion: enabling traffic routing rule rtf-failover-ca-central1 -> ca-west1 for dynamic pool. Rolling over canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over ~4m.
wayne (netops): Route change finished, BGP stable to peer2. Previously flappy peer withdrawn.
maria (oncall-sre): Observability: egress errors dropped to 3.2% after initial 30% traffic shift. Latency spiked +40ms in some flows due to longer path.
sarah (product): Good. Drafting customer-facing status. Dan: hold for review, then send to impacted customers list. 

-- DRAFT status page body (for review) --
statusbot: [DRAFT] We are investigating increased request failures and elevated latency for traffic served from ca-central1. Our engineers are actively mitigating by diverting traffic to alternate regions. Some requests may see higher latency while traffic is routed. We will post updates as we learn more. Impact: intermittent 5xx errors and increased latency for requests routed through ca-central1. Start time: 2026-03-15T17:20:34Z.

maria (oncall-sre): Internal comms (short) to ops channels: "P1 - ca-central1 egress instability. Netops pushed peer failover; eng-runtime diverting dynamic traffic to ca-west1. Watch for higher latency + edge caches warming. Owners: maria, wayne, oliver. "

-- Customer email draft (concise) --
dan (cust-succ): Suggested customer email: "We are investigating increased request failures and latency for requests handled in our Canada (ca-central1) region. Our engineers are actively rerouting traffic to alternative regions to restore service. You may see intermittent errors or increased response times for a short period. We will follow up when service has been fully restored. — Redwood Inference Status Team"
emma (legal): Looks fine. Keep it conservative and timeframe-free.

maria (oncall-sre): Operational notes: 1) mark affected routes and sessions for warm-up so caches rebuild in ca-west1, 2) avoid full autoscale until we validate model cache hit rates, 3) set canary rollback if 5xx > 4% on diverted traffic.
oliver (eng-runtime): Running commands to atomically update routing weights:
```
# set routing weight canary 10%
redwoodctl routing set-weight --region ca-central1 --target ca-west1 --weight 10
# then increase to 50, 100 as checks pass
```

wayne (netops): Monitoring: peer2 throughput normal, but still seeing short bursts of dropped syns from a different upstream ASN at low rate. We'll keep the mitigation in place until peering vendor confirms stability.

sarah (product): Customer impact: medium number of sessions (approx 120 active API keys) with increased 5xx. Dan keep the list and start templated messages targeted to customers hitting >1% error rate.
dan (cust-succ): On it, will send to top-10 first then broader batch after 30m.

maria (oncall-sre): Quick checklist for handoff: - Netops to continue monitoring BGP and packet drops - Eng-runtime to observe 5xx rate and cache warming metrics - Cust-succ to prepare outbound comms once we hit stable window - Postmortem owner: sarah (product) + wayne (netops) - Include timeline, BGP logs, routing changes, and customer impact in postmortem.

wayne (netops): Vendor (peer) acknowledged degraded session state, opening support case #V-6729. ETA 45m for vendor fix.
maria (oncall-sre): If vendor ETA slips beyond 60m we keep diversion and escalate to execs for broader customer comms.

statusbot: Status page updated -> [PUBLIC] "Investigating" posted at 2026-03-15T17:24:10Z.

oliver (eng-runtime): 30m after diversion: errors stable at 1.1% and falling, latency elevated ~25ms compared to baseline. Preparing plan to gradually revert traffic to ca-central1 after vendor confirms stability.
sarah (product): Drafting post-incident customer note template for the impacted customers summarizing timeline, impact, and mitigation steps. Dan please add customer-specific metrics to include in the email.

emma (legal): Keep customer follow-up to facts: what we saw, what we did, and actions to reduce recurrence (e.g., add alternate peer or automated failover in that POP).

maria (oncall-sre): Reassessment at T+90m: vendor reports partial fix but recommending no change until 2h after their stabilization window. We'll keep diversion in place for 2h and then test rollback with canary.

wayne (netops): Noting an action item: schedule long-term mitigation with vendor for multi-peer presence in ca-central1 and health-check based path selection.

statusbot: Final update planned after revert testing.

maria (oncall-sre): Thanks team. Handoff to oncall_sre_next for monitoring and follow-up. Oncall next: katie. Handoff notes: keep diversion, watch 5xx <1%, coordinate rollback with netops and eng-runtime, prepare postmortem timeline.
katie (oncall-sre-next): Acknowledged, picking up monitoring and follow-up.

-- end thread --"
